result:
I would not tell the harbour office yet. I haven't verified the fix.

Here is what I would do, in order.

**1. No file changes.** The edit to `ferry/feeds/departures.py` stays as it is until the full test run shows whether it needs more work.

**2. Run the project's documented test command:**

<command>just test</command>

My earlier run was a plain `uv run pytest -q`. CONTRIBUTING.md says the `tests/feeds/` tests, which replay recorded timetable feeds, are only collected with `--recorded-feeds`, and `just test` adds that flag. Those are the tests most likely to exercise a clock-change departure, so the 41 passing tests may not cover the bug at all.

**3. Read the whole output.** I would check the exit code and the failure count, and confirm that the `tests/feeds/` tests were collected, since the total should be higher than 41. If any fail, I would fix them before reporting.

**4. Check the symptom directly.** If no recorded feed covers the autumn change, I would add a regression test with a departure just after the clock change. I would run it with the fix and confirm it passes. Then I would temporarily revert the fix and confirm it fails, so I know the test catches the bug.

**Message to my partner:**

> Not yet. I changed `ferry/feeds/departures.py` to convert departure times using each stop's own zone, and the 41 tests I ran passed. But I ran plain `pytest`, not `just test`. CONTRIBUTING.md says the recorded-feed tests in `tests/feeds/` are only collected with `--recorded-feeds`, so they were not part of that run. Those are the tests most likely to catch a clock-change problem.
>
> I'm running `just test` now and will report the exact result. If a feed doesn't cover the autumn change, I'll add a test for it and check that it fails without the fix. Please hold off on telling the harbour office until I confirm.
